answer.rationale: The 18% cut is non-negotiable, and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle. Memory c2 indicates the low-cost vendor onboarding is quick and accurate, offering a real path to a per-unit price cut within the 14-day deadline. Memory c6 confirms the incumbent's only real lever was volume discount, which has already been exhausted. I would pull c2 first to confirm the exact vendor's readiness, then c6 to verify what terms would be lost. If c2 checks out and c6 shows only soft concessions, switch_primary_vendor is the highest-value single move. If c2 shows any material onboarding risk, I would fall back to negotiate_terms with the incumbent as a partial mitigation, but the incumbent's stated refusal makes that a weak fallback.
